title: Booking, proctoring and the rules of the day

blocks.text: Booking, proctoring and the rules of the day
**Level:** Foundations · **Module 11:** Exam readiness 1 · **Page 2 of 5** **Exams:** all

**After this page you can** book an exam, prepare for online proctoring or a test centre, request an accommodation in the right order, plan around retakes, and keep a credential current through renewal.

Checked against the Associate, Developer, Architect Foundations and Architect Professional exam guides (version 1.0, effective July 2026; the registration, policy and renewal sections are the same in all four), the Anthropic Certification Terms and Conditions, the Anthropic Certification Exam Policy (last updated 25 June 2026), the Pearson VUE pages for Anthropic exams and for online proctoring, and the Anthropic announcement of the programme, all read on 2026-10-02, and the facts on this page re-checked against the official pages on 2026-10-05. **Fees, rules and deadlines change; read the current guide, the Terms, the Exam Policy and your booking confirmation before you rely on anything here.**
Why it matters

A candidate can know the material and still lose the fee: a name that does not match the ID, a booking changed too late, a second monitor on the desk, an accommodation requested after scheduling. These are rules, not judgment calls, and each is written down. Reading them once costs less than one forfeited fee.
The idea
The booking path

items: **Check eligibility and pick the exam** (page 1): at least 18, a valid government ID, and employment at a Claude Partner Network organisation with a recognised company e-mail domain. Some countries and regions have restrictions, so check the exam policy.
**Read the three documents before you pay**: the exam guide, the Certification Terms and Conditions and the Certification Exam Policy. The guide tells you to read them before registering.

**Register and pay.** The fee shown at checkout reflects any discount for your partner tier. Fees on 2026-10-02: Associate 99, Developer and Architect Foundations 125, Architect Professional 175 (USD).
**Create your Pearson VUE account** from the confirmation instructions and sign in to schedule.
**Choose a date and a delivery mode:** online proctoring or a Pearson test centre.

**Cancel or reschedule on time.** Cancel or reschedule at least **48 hours** before the appointment, for online and test-centre bookings alike. Inside 48 hours the fee is forfeited. Read your confirmation email, which governs your booking.
**Do not no-show, and do not arrive late.** A candidate who does not appear, or who arrives after the permitted late-arrival window, forfeits the fee and must register again.

blocks.text: Your name and your ID

The name on your registration must match your ID exactly. On exam day you must show a valid, unexpired, government-issued photo ID; if the name differs, you may be refused entry and lose the fee. If a name needs correcting, do it **before** you schedule, through the certifications support contact given in the guide. Impersonation, including using an ID that is not yours, is misconduct.
Online proctoring or a test centre
Both modes follow the same rules of conduct. They differ in logistics.

rows: Run Pearson's system test on the computer and connection; find a private, distraction-free space
Travel there; arrive in time for the late-arrival window
You consent to monitoring by human proctors and assistive AI tools for the whole test, and must stay within view of the proctor and webcam
Pearson's page lists the domains your network must allow for the online test, so check any firewall in advance

blocks.text: Choose by risk. If your home or office cannot give a quiet room, one monitor, a reliable connection and no interruptions, a test centre removes four ways to fail for non-knowledge reasons.
The rules of the day

During the exam you **must**: stay in view of the proctor and webcam if online; keep your workspace clear of notes, books, phones, secondary monitors and other materials; not talk to anyone; and not capture, copy or reproduce any exam content. The Exam Policy adds that prohibited behaviour includes **using AI products or services to help you during the exam**, having more than one monitor, possessing electronic devices or notes (including during breaks), taking unscheduled breaks unless approved in advance, and misrepresenting your country of residence or where the exam is delivered. Permitted items, such as scratch paper, are set by Pearson VUE.

**Consequences.** Anthropic may suspend or ban you, require a retake, invalidate your result, not issue or revoke the credential, and keep the fee. You can appeal a final decision within 14 calendar days of notice, through the programme (first through the third-party provider where one runs it). The standard-setting outcome and the content of individual items are not open to appeal.

**Confidentiality.** Before the exam begins you accept a non-disclosure agreement covering all questions, options and scenarios. If you decline, the session ends and no refund is given. Afterwards you may not describe the questions. You can describe your preparation, and the course's own questions are written fresh for that reason.
Accommodations: the order matters

Reasonable accommodations are available for documented disabilities or needs, in line with applicable law. The sequence is fixed: **request the accommodation through Pearson VUE, wait for approval, and only then schedule the exam.** Both the Exam Policy and the guide say the request must be submitted and approved before scheduling. Extra time or a break you did not arrange in advance is not available on the day, and an unapproved break counts as misconduct.
If you do not pass

Retake waiting periods grow with each failed attempt: **14 days after the first, 30 days after the second, 90 days after the third**, with at most **four attempts in a rolling 12 months per exam**. Each attempt costs the full fee. Not passing one exam does not block another. Use the percent-correct by domain on the score report to aim your revision: it tells you where to study, though it does not decide the result. Retake only when you have changed something about how you prepare; the mock exams and review bank in this module are for that.
The credential: validity, renewal and the badge

items: **Renewing on time.** Before it expires you review what has changed and complete a **free, non-proctored assessment** on the Anthropic Partner Academy; there is no fee. If the exam content changes significantly, Anthropic may instead require holders to retake the full exam.
**If it lapses.** You must retake the full exam at the full fee. The Exam Policy states that once a certification has expired you can no longer renew it and must re-earn it.

**The badge.** Anthropic's announcement says digital badges are issued through Credly by Pearson. A credential is a statement of the period it covers: under the Terms you must not present yourself as currently certified after it expires, and you should list the certification period. The Terms also say a certification is not a warranty of your abilities, so do not describe it as one.

**Partners and revocation.** Certification belongs to the individual, not to the partner organisation. Anthropic may revoke a certification for breach of the Terms, misconduct or other reasons the Terms list, such as a risk to the programme's integrity.

blocks.text: Traps

items: **Scheduling first, asking for an accommodation later.** The approval must come before the booking, and it cannot be arranged on the day.
**Changing a booking late.** Cancel or reschedule at least 48 hours ahead, whichever mode you chose; inside 48 hours the fee is forfeited.
**Treating an expired credential as renewable.** Renewal is before expiry and by the free assessment; after a lapse the full exam is needed.
